title: Creation of heavens and earth
scene: Light breaking over dark primeval waters at the dawn of creation, the first light dividing from darkness
setting: the ancient Near East at the dawn of history: primeval landscapes, rivers, gardens and open plains

title: Creation of Adam and Eve
scene: A lush garden in Eden with rivers and trees in soft morning light; the first man and woman seen small and at a distance among the foliage
setting: the ancient Near East at the dawn of history: primeval landscapes, rivers, gardens and open plains

title: The fall and expulsion
scene: The fall and expulsion: The serpent questions what God said to the woman in the garden of Eden. She and the man eat the fruit of the tree God told them not to eat, and everything changes.
setting: the ancient Near East at the dawn of history: primeval landscapes, rivers, gardens and open plains

title: Cain and Abel
scene: Cain and Abel: Adam and Eve's sons bring offerings to the Lord. God accepts Abel's offering and not Cain's, and Cain's anger leads to the first murder.
setting: the ancient Near East at the dawn of history: primeval landscapes, rivers, gardens and open plains

title: Descendants of Cain and Seth
scene: Descendants of Cain and Seth: Two family lines follow the first murder: Cain's descendants, among them the first city-builder, musicians and metalworkers, and the line of Seth from Adam to Noah. Methuselah and Enoch, who, appear here.
setting: the ancient Near East at the dawn of history: primeval landscapes, rivers, gardens and open plains

title: Corruption before the flood
scene: Corruption before the flood: The earth is filled with wickedness, and the Lord is grieved that he made man. Only Noah finds grace in his eyes. in the KJV here means that God was sorry or grieved.
setting: the ancient Near East at the dawn of history: primeval landscapes, rivers, gardens and open plains

title: Noah builds the ark
scene: Noah builds the ark: The earth is filled with violence, but Noah finds grace in the eyes of the Lord. God tells him to build an ark and bring his family and the animals into it.
setting: the ancient Near East at the dawn of history: primeval landscapes, rivers, gardens and open plains

title: The great flood
scene: The great flood: The waters rise over the earth for many days and every living thing outside the ark perishes. Then God remembers Noah, the waters go down, the ark rests on the mountains of Ararat, and a dove is sent out.
setting: the ancient Near East at the dawn of history: primeval landscapes, rivers, gardens and open plains

title: God's covenant with Noah
scene: God's covenant with Noah: After the flood Noah builds an altar. God promises never again to destroy the earth by a flood, and sets his bow in the cloud as the sign of the covenant.
setting: the ancient Near East at the dawn of history: primeval landscapes, rivers, gardens and open plains

title: Noah and his sons
scene: Noah and his sons: Noah plants a vineyard and becomes drunk. How his sons Shem, Ham and Japheth respond leads to Noah's blessing and his curse on Canaan, Ham's son.
setting: the ancient Near East at the dawn of history: primeval landscapes, rivers, gardens and open plains

title: Tower of Babel
scene: Tower of Babel: The whole earth has one language. People on the plain of Shinar set out to build a city and a tower reaching to heaven, to make a name for themselves.
setting: the ancient Near East at the dawn of history: primeval landscapes, rivers, gardens and open plains

title: Call of Abram
scene: Call of Abram: God tells Abram to leave his country and his father's house for a land God will show him, and promises to make of him a great nation through whom all families of the earth will be blessed.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Abram in Egypt
scene: Abram in Egypt: Famine drives Abram to Egypt. Afraid for his life, he says that Sarai his wife is his sister, and Pharaoh takes her into his house until the Lord sends plagues.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Abram rescues Lot
scene: Abram rescues Lot: Abram and his nephew Lot part ways, and Lot settles near Sodom. When kings capture Lot in a war, Abram rescues him and is blessed by Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Covenant with Abram
scene: Covenant with Abram: Abram is still childless. God tells him to look at the stars and count them, and Abram believes the Lord. God then makes a covenant with him in a solemn ceremony.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Hagar and Ishmael
scene: Hagar and Ishmael: Sarai, still without children, gives her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram. Hagar conceives and flees from Sarai's harsh treatment, and the angel of the Lord meets her by a spring in the wilderness.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Covenant of circumcision
scene: Covenant of circumcision: God renames Abram as Abraham and Sarai as Sarah, promises that Sarah will bear a son, and gives circumcision as the sign of the covenant. Abraham laughs at the thought of a child at his age.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Three visitors and promise of Isaac
scene: Three visitors and promise of Isaac: Three men visit Abraham's tent at Mamre in the heat of the day, and he hurries to welcome them. One of them says Sarah will have a son, and Sarah, listening at the tent door, laughs.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Abraham intercedes for Sodom
scene: Abraham intercedes for Sodom: The Lord tells Abraham that the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great. Abraham asks whether he will spare the city for fifty righteous people, then forty-five, down to ten.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
scene: Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: Two angels come to Sodom, where Lot takes them in and the men of the city surround his house. At dawn the angels lead Lot's family out, fire and brimstone fall, and Lot's wife looks back.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Lot and his daughters
scene: Lot and his daughters: After Sodom's destruction, Lot and his two daughters live in a cave. This short and troubling account explains the origins of the Moabites and the Ammonites.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Abraham and Abimelech
scene: Abraham and Abimelech: In Gerar, Abraham again says that Sarah is his sister, and King Abimelech takes her. God warns Abimelech in a dream, and he returns Sarah to Abraham.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Birth of Isaac
scene: Birth of Isaac: The Lord does as he promised, and Sarah bears Abraham a son in his old age. They name him Isaac, which means laughter, and Sarah says.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Hagar and Ishmael sent away
scene: Hagar and Ishmael sent away: At the feast for Isaac's weaning, Sarah sees Ishmael mocking and asks Abraham to send him and Hagar away. In the wilderness of Beersheba the water runs out, and God hears the boy's voice.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Abraham tested with Isaac
scene: Abraham tested with Isaac: God tells Abraham to take his son Isaac, whom he loves, to a mountain in the land of Moriah and offer him there. This is one of the most searching stories in Genesis.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Death and burial of Sarah
scene: Death and burial of Sarah: Sarah dies at Hebron aged 127. Abraham, a stranger in the land, buys the cave of Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite as a burying place, his first owned ground in Canaan.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Rebekah chosen for Isaac
scene: Rebekah chosen for Isaac: Abraham sends his servant to his family's homeland to find a wife for Isaac. At the well, the servant prays for a sign, and Rebekah offers water for him and his camels.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Birth of Esau and Jacob
scene: Birth of Esau and Jacob: Rebekah's twins struggle within her, and she is told that the elder will serve the younger. Years later Esau, hungry from the field, sells his birthright to Jacob for bread and lentil pottage.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Isaac and Abimelech
scene: Isaac and Abimelech: During a famine Isaac lives in Gerar and the Lord renews to him the promises made to Abraham. Isaac's wells cause disputes with the Philistine herdsmen until he digs one at Rehoboth.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Jacob receives Isaac's blessing
scene: Jacob receives Isaac's blessing: Isaac, old and blind, plans to bless Esau. Rebekah and Jacob use goatskins and Esau's clothes to deceive him, and Jacob receives the blessing instead. Esau vows to kill his brother.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Jacob's dream at Bethel
scene: Jacob's dream at Bethel: Fleeing from Esau, Jacob sleeps on the way with a stone for a pillow. He dreams of a ladder reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending, and the Lord renews his promise.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Jacob meets Rachel and marries
scene: Jacob meets Rachel and marries: At a well in Haran, Jacob meets Rachel, daughter of his uncle Laban. He serves seven years for her, but on the wedding night Laban gives him Leah instead.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Jacob's children
scene: Jacob's children: Leah, Rachel and their maids Bilhah and Zilpah bear Jacob eleven sons and a daughter. Each name records the mother's feelings, ending with Rachel's son Joseph.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Jacob prospers and departs
scene: Jacob prospers and departs: Jacob's flocks grow while Laban keeps changing his wages. Jacob leaves secretly for Canaan with his family, Laban pursues him, and they make a covenant at a heap of stones.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Jacob wrestles with God
scene: Jacob wrestles with God: Jacob prepares to meet Esau and prays for deliverance. At the ford Jabbok a man wrestles with him until daybreak. Jacob is given the name Israel and calls the place Peniel.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Jacob and Esau reconcile
scene: Jacob and Esau reconcile: Jacob bows seven times as he approaches Esau, but Esau runs to meet him, embraces him and weeps. The brothers part in peace.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Dinah and Shechem
scene: Dinah and Shechem: Jacob's daughter Dinah is taken and humbled by Shechem, a local prince. Her brothers Simeon and Levi take a violent revenge on the city, and Jacob rebukes them.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Return to Bethel and Rachel's death
scene: Return to Bethel and Rachel's death: God sends Jacob back to Bethel, where he puts away foreign gods and builds an altar. On the road to Bethlehem, Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin, and Isaac dies at Hebron.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Joseph's dreams and betrayal
scene: Joseph's dreams and betrayal: Jacob loves Joseph more than his other sons and gives him a coat of many colours. Joseph's dreams of his family bowing to him deepen his brothers' hatred, and they sell him to traders bound for Egypt.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Judah and Tamar
scene: Judah and Tamar: An interruption in Joseph's story: Judah fails to keep his promise to his widowed daughter-in-law Tamar, and she takes matters into her own hands. Her son Pharez is later an ancestor of David.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Joseph and Potiphar's wife
scene: Joseph and Potiphar's wife: In Egypt, Joseph serves in the house of Potiphar, and the Lord prospers everything he does. Potiphar's wife tries to seduce him, and when he refuses she accuses him falsely. He is put in prison.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Joseph interprets prison dreams
scene: Joseph interprets prison dreams: In prison, Pharaoh's butler and baker each have a dream. Joseph says that interpretations belong to God and explains both dreams, which come true, but the butler forgets him.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams
scene: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams: Pharaoh dreams of seven fat and seven lean cattle, and no one can explain it. The butler remembers Joseph, who foretells seven years of plenty and seven of famine and is made ruler over Egypt.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Joseph's brothers travel to Egypt
scene: Joseph's brothers travel to Egypt: Famine reaches Canaan, and Jacob sends ten sons to buy grain in Egypt. Joseph recognises his brothers, though they do not recognise him, and he accuses them of being spies.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Benjamin goes to Egypt
scene: Benjamin goes to Egypt: The grain runs out and the brothers must return to Egypt with Benjamin, Jacob's youngest son. Joseph welcomes them to a meal in his house and has to leave the room to weep.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Joseph tests his brothers
scene: Joseph tests his brothers: Joseph has his silver cup hidden in Benjamin's sack, and Benjamin is accused of theft. Judah offers to stay as a slave in his place, for their father's sake.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Joseph reveals his identity
scene: Joseph reveals his identity: Years after his brothers sold him into slavery, Joseph is ruler over Egypt. His brothers stand before him without knowing who he is, until he can no longer hold back.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Jacob's family moves to Egypt
scene: Jacob's family moves to Egypt: God tells Jacob not to fear going down to Egypt. Jacob's family of seventy settles in the land of Goshen, Jacob blesses Pharaoh, and Joseph manages Egypt through the famine.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Jacob blesses Ephraim and Manasseh
scene: Jacob blesses Ephraim and Manasseh: Jacob, near death, adopts Joseph's two sons as his own. He crosses his hands to put his right hand on the younger, Ephraim, and his left on the elder, Manasseh.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Jacob blesses his sons
scene: Jacob blesses his sons: Jacob gathers his twelve sons and speaks to each of them in poetry about what will befall them. Judah is told that the sceptre shall not depart from him.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Death of Jacob and Joseph
scene: Death of Jacob and Joseph: Jacob is buried in Canaan with great mourning. His sons fear Joseph's revenge, but Joseph answers, Joseph dies in Egypt.
setting: Bronze Age Canaan, Mesopotamia and Egypt: tent-dwelling herders with flocks, wells and hill country

title: Israel oppressed in Egypt
scene: Israel oppressed in Egypt: A new king arises who does not know Joseph. Fearing Israel's growing numbers, he makes them slaves and orders the Hebrew midwives to kill the baby boys, but the midwives fear God.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Birth and rescue of Moses
scene: Birth and rescue of Moses: A Levite mother hides her baby boy and then sets him in an ark of bulrushes on the Nile. Pharaoh's daughter finds him, and his sister arranges for his own mother to nurse him.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Moses flees to Midian
scene: Moses flees to Midian: Grown up, Moses kills an Egyptian he sees beating a Hebrew, and he flees to Midian. There he helps the daughters of a priest at a well, marries Zipporah, and God hears Israel's groaning.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Burning bush
scene: Moses, a shepherd, kneeling barefoot before a desert bush that burns with bright fire yet is not consumed, at the foot of a mountain, his flock nearby
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks
must_show: the bush burning but not consumed

title: Moses confronts Pharaoh
scene: Moses confronts Pharaoh: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let Israel go. Pharaoh answers, and makes their work harder, and the people blame Moses. God renews his promise, and Aaron's rod becomes a serpent.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Plagues of Egypt
scene: Plagues of Egypt: Pharaoh refuses to let Israel go. Ten plagues follow, from water turned to blood to the death of the firstborn. These chapters tell the first nine and the warning of the tenth.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: First Passover
scene: First Passover: Before the last plague, God tells each household in Israel to kill a lamb and put its blood on the doorposts, and to eat the meal ready to leave. Israel is told to keep this day as a feast for ever.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Exodus from Egypt
scene: Exodus from Egypt: At midnight the firstborn of Egypt die, and Pharaoh at last tells Israel to go. The people leave in haste with their unleavened dough, after 430 years in Egypt.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Consecration and guidance
scene: Consecration and guidance: God claims every firstborn as his, and Moses gives instructions for remembering the exodus. God leads the people the long way, by a pillar of cloud by day and of fire by night.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Crossing the Red Sea
scene: Crossing the Red Sea: Israel has left Egypt, but Pharaoh's army pursues them to the edge of the sea. Moses tells the people to stand still and see the salvation of the Lord.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Song of Moses and Miriam
scene: Song of Moses and Miriam: On the far side of the sea, Moses and Israel sing to the Lord. Miriam the prophetess takes a timbrel and the women answer her with dancing.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Bitter water made sweet
scene: Bitter water made sweet: Three days into the wilderness the people find only bitter water at Marah, and they murmur. The Lord shows Moses a tree which makes the water sweet, and they come to Elim with its twelve wells.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Manna and quail
scene: Manna and quail: The hungry people complain. God sends quails in the evening and, in the morning, manna, a small round thing on the ground. Each day's gathering is enough, with a double portion before the sabbath.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Water from the rock
scene: Water from the rock: At Rephidim there is no water and the people quarrel with Moses. God tells him to strike the rock in Horeb, and water comes out. The place is named Massah and Meribah.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Battle with Amalek
scene: Battle with Amalek: Amalek attacks Israel at Rephidim. Joshua leads the fight while Moses holds up his hands on the hilltop, with Aaron and Hur supporting them until sunset.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Jethro advises Moses
scene: Jethro advises Moses: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, sees Moses judging the people from morning to evening. He advises him to appoint able men as rulers over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: God at Mount Sinai
scene: God at Mount Sinai: Israel camps before mount Sinai. God offers to make them, and comes down on the mountain in fire, smoke, thunder and the sound of a trumpet.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Ten Commandments
scene: Ten Commandments: At mount Sinai, with thunder and lightning on the mountain, God speaks the ten commandments to Israel.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Covenant confirmed
scene: Covenant confirmed: The people promise to do all the Lord has said. Moses sprinkles the blood of the covenant, and the elders see the God of Israel. Moses goes up into the cloud for forty days and nights.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Tabernacle instructions
scene: Tabernacle instructions: On the mountain God gives Moses the pattern for the tabernacle, a portable sanctuary: the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altar, the priests' garments and the craftsmen Bezaleel and Aholiab.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Golden calf
scene: Golden calf: While Moses is on the mountain, the people ask Aaron to make them gods. He makes a calf of gold, and Moses comes down to find them worshipping it.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Moses intercedes and sees God's glory
scene: Moses intercedes and sees God's glory: After the golden calf, Moses pleads for the people and asks to see God's glory. God passes by, proclaiming his name, and renews the covenant on new tables of stone.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Building the tabernacle
scene: Building the tabernacle: The people bring so many offerings that Moses has to stop them. The craftsmen make everything as commanded, the tabernacle is set up, and the glory of the Lord fills it.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Ordination of Aaron and sons
scene: Ordination of Aaron and sons: Moses washes, clothes and anoints Aaron and his sons as priests before the whole congregation, and they stay at the door of the tabernacle for seven days of consecration.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: First priestly offerings
scene: First priestly offerings: On the eighth day Aaron offers the first sacrifices. He blesses the people, the glory of the Lord appears, and fire comes out from before the Lord to consume the offering.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Nadab and Abihu
scene: Nadab and Abihu: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu offer that the Lord had not commanded, and fire from the Lord devours them. Aaron holds his peace.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Day of Atonement instructions
scene: Day of Atonement instructions: God gives instructions for the yearly Day of Atonement. The high priest enters the holy place within the veil, and one goat is offered while the other, the scapegoat, is sent into the wilderness.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Holiness and covenant blessings
scene: Holiness and covenant blessings: These chapters, sometimes called the Holiness Code, teach Israel to be holy. They include, the feasts, the jubilee, and blessings and warnings.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Israel's camp and census
scene: Israel's camp and census: A year after leaving Egypt, Moses counts the men of Israel able to go to war, tribe by tribe. The tribes are arranged around the tabernacle, and the Levites are given its care.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Dedication of the tabernacle
scene: Dedication of the tabernacle: When the tabernacle is set up, the leader of each tribe brings an identical offering on twelve successive days. Moses then hears the voice speaking from above the mercy seat.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Departure from Sinai
scene: Departure from Sinai: The cloud covers the tabernacle, and Israel moves or stays as it moves or stays. Silver trumpets are made, and Israel sets out from Sinai with the ark going before them.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Complaints and quail
scene: Complaints and quail: The people complain about the manna and long for the fish and vegetables of Egypt. Moses feels the burden is too heavy, God shares his spirit with seventy elders, and quails arrive in great numbers.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Miriam and Aaron oppose Moses
scene: Miriam and Aaron oppose Moses: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses, asking whether the Lord has spoken only by him. God defends Moses, and Miriam is struck with leprosy for seven days.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Twelve spies in Canaan
scene: Twelve spies in Canaan: Moses sends twelve men to spy out Canaan. They bring back a cluster of grapes carried on a pole and report a land flowing with milk and honey, but ten of them say the people there are too strong.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Israel refuses to enter
scene: Israel refuses to enter: The people weep all night and want to return to Egypt. Joshua and Caleb plead with them to trust the Lord. God declares that this generation will wander forty years in the wilderness.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Korah's rebellion
scene: Korah's rebellion: Korah, Dathan and Abiram lead a rebellion against Moses and Aaron. The ground opens and swallows the leaders, and Aaron stands between the dead and the living to stop a plague.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Aaron's budding staff
scene: Aaron's budding staff: To settle who God has chosen as priest, a rod from each tribe is laid in the tabernacle. Overnight Aaron's rod buds, blossoms and yields almonds.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Moses strikes the rock
scene: Moses strikes the rock: Miriam dies, and at Kadesh there is no water. God tells Moses to speak to the rock, but Moses strikes it twice. Water flows, but God says Moses and Aaron will not bring Israel into the land.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Death of Aaron
scene: Death of Aaron: At mount Hor, Moses strips Aaron of his priestly garments and puts them on his son Eleazar. Aaron dies on the mountain, and Israel mourns him thirty days.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Bronze serpent
scene: Bronze serpent: The people speak against God and Moses, and fiery serpents bite them. God tells Moses to make a serpent of brass and set it on a pole, and whoever looks at it lives. Jesus refers to this in John 3:14.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Balaam and Balak
scene: Balaam and Balak: Balak, king of Moab, hires the prophet Balaam to curse Israel. On the way Balaam's ass sees the angel of the Lord before he does. Each time Balaam opens his mouth, he blesses Israel instead.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Sin at Peor and Phinehas
scene: Sin at Peor and Phinehas: At Shittim the men of Israel join in the worship of Baal-peor with Moabite women, and a plague breaks out. Phinehas, Aaron's grandson, acts zealously and the plague is stayed.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Daughters of Zelophehad
scene: Daughters of Zelophehad: Zelophehad has died with no sons. His five daughters ask for their father's inheritance, Moses brings their case to the Lord, and God says they speak right.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Moses asks for a shepherd for Israel
scene: Moses asks for a shepherd for Israel: God tells Moses to view the land from the mountain, for he will not enter it. Moses asks God to set a man over the people. Joshua is chosen.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: War against Midian
scene: War against Midian: Israel goes to war against Midian after the sin at Peor. The chapter also gives rules for purification after battle and for dividing the spoil.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Reuben and Gad settle east of Jordan
scene: Reuben and Gad settle east of Jordan: The tribes of Reuben and Gad, rich in cattle, ask to settle in the land east of the Jordan. Moses agrees on condition that their men cross over and fight alongside their brothers first.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Moses recalls the wilderness
scene: Moses recalls the wilderness: Deuteronomy opens with Moses speaking to Israel on the plains of Moab. He recalls their journey from Horeb, the refusal at Kadesh, and the victories over Sihon and Og.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: The Shema and covenant teaching
scene: The Shema and covenant teaching: Moses calls Israel to love God with all their heart, soul and might, and to teach his words to their children.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Blessings and curses
scene: Blessings and curses: Moses sets before Israel blessing and cursing, life and death. Ending with a call to choose life, these chapters lay out what faithfulness and unfaithfulness to the covenant will bring.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Joshua succeeds Moses
scene: Joshua succeeds Moses: Moses, now 120, tells Israel he will not cross the Jordan. He charges Joshua to be strong and of a good courage, and writes the law and gives it to the priests to be read every seven years.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Song of Moses
scene: Song of Moses: Moses speaks a song in the ears of all Israel, a poem that praises God as the Rock and warns Israel of turning away. Afterwards God tells Moses to climb mount Nebo.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Moses blesses the tribes
scene: Moses blesses the tribes: Before his death, Moses blesses each tribe of Israel in turn. He ends,
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: Death of Moses
scene: Death of Moses: Moses climbs mount Nebo, and the Lord shows him the whole land. Moses dies there and God buries him, and no man knows his grave. Israel mourns thirty days, and Joshua leads them.
setting: ancient Egypt and the Sinai wilderness: desert mountains and the Israelite tribes with tents and flocks

title: The Lord commissions Joshua
scene: The Lord commissions Joshua: After Moses' death the Lord tells Joshua to lead Israel over the Jordan. Three times he is told to, and to keep the book of the law.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Rahab and the spies
scene: Rahab and the spies: Joshua sends two spies to Jericho, and Rahab hides them on her roof. She says the people's hearts have melted for fear of Israel's God, and she asks for her family's safety. A scarlet cord marks her house.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Crossing the Jordan
scene: Crossing the Jordan: The priests carry the ark into the Jordan at flood season, and the waters stand up in a heap. Israel crosses on dry ground, and twelve stones from the river are set up as a memorial.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Circumcision and Passover at Gilgal
scene: Circumcision and Passover at Gilgal: At Gilgal, the men born in the wilderness are circumcised and Israel keeps the Passover. The next day they eat the produce of the land, and the manna stops.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Fall of Jericho
scene: Fall of Jericho: Joshua meets the captain of the Lord's host near Jericho. Israel is told to march around the shut-up city once a day for six days, and seven times on the seventh.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Achan's sin and defeat at Ai
scene: Achan's sin and defeat at Ai: Israel is defeated at the small town of Ai. Joshua falls on his face before the ark, and the cause is traced to Achan, who took things from Jericho that were devoted to God.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Victory at Ai
scene: Victory at Ai: Joshua takes Ai by an ambush. Afterwards he builds an altar on mount Ebal and reads all the words of the law to the people, as Moses had commanded.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Gibeonite deception
scene: Gibeonite deception: The Gibeonites pretend to come from a far country, with old sacks and mouldy bread, and Israel makes a treaty with them without asking counsel of the Lord.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Sun stands still and southern campaign
scene: Sun stands still and southern campaign: Five Amorite kings attack Gibeon, and Joshua comes to its defence. Great hailstones fall, and at Joshua's word the sun stands still over Gibeon. Israel then takes the southern cities.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Northern campaign
scene: Northern campaign: The kings of the north gather at the waters of Merom with horses and chariots. Joshua defeats them and takes Hazor.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Division of the land
scene: Division of the land: The land is divided among the tribes by lot. Caleb receives Hebron at eighty-five, cities of refuge are set apart, and the Levites receive cities. These chapters close with.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Eastern tribes' altar
scene: Eastern tribes' altar: The tribes east of the Jordan go home and build a great altar by the river. The other tribes prepare for war, fearing rebellion, until they learn it is a witness and not an altar for sacrifice.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Joshua's farewell and covenant renewal
scene: Joshua's farewell and covenant renewal: Old Joshua gathers Israel at Shechem and recounts what God has done. He says,
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Incomplete conquest
scene: Incomplete conquest: After Joshua's death the tribes fail to drive out the peoples of the land. A new generation arises that does not know the Lord, setting up the cycle of the book of Judges: sin, oppression, crying out, deliverance.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Othniel delivers Israel
scene: Othniel delivers Israel: Israel serves other gods and falls under the king of Mesopotamia for eight years. When they cry to the Lord, the Spirit of the Lord comes on Othniel, Caleb's nephew, who delivers them.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Ehud and Eglon
scene: Ehud and Eglon: Israel serves Eglon, king of Moab. Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite, brings tribute to Eglon, asks for a private audience, and kills him with a hidden dagger.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Shamgar
scene: Shamgar: A single verse: Shamgar the son of Anath kills six hundred Philistines with an ox goad, and he also delivers Israel.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Deborah and Barak
scene: Deborah and Barak: Under Jabin of Canaan and his captain Sisera, Israel is oppressed for twenty years. Deborah, a prophetess judging Israel, sends Barak to battle. Sisera flees and dies by the hand of Jael. Chapter 5 is Deborah's song.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Gideon's call
scene: Gideon's call: Midian raids Israel's crops every year. The angel of the Lord finds Gideon threshing wheat in hiding and calls him a mighty man of valour. Gideon tears down his father's altar to Baal and asks for signs with a fleece.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Gideon's 300
scene: Gideon's 300: God reduces Gideon's army from 32,000 to 300 so that Israel will not boast. At night they break pitchers, show lamps and blow trumpets, crying.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Gideon's aftermath
scene: Gideon's aftermath: Gideon pursues the Midianite kings and deals with towns that refused him help. He refuses to be king, but makes an ephod from the gold spoil, and it becomes a snare to Israel.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Abimelech's rise and fall
scene: Abimelech's rise and fall: Gideon's son Abimelech kills his seventy brothers and makes himself king at Shechem. Jotham, the youngest, escapes and tells a parable of trees choosing a king. Abimelech's reign ends in violence.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Tola and Jair
scene: Tola and Jair: Two brief notes about judges: Tola of Issachar judges Israel twenty-three years, and Jair of Gilead judges twenty-two years. Jair had thirty sons who rode on thirty ass colts.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Jephthah and his vow
scene: Jephthah and his vow: Jephthah, an outcast, is called back to lead Gilead against Ammon. Before battle he vows to offer whatever first comes out of his house to meet him, and his daughter comes out with timbrels.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Ibzan Elon and Abdon
scene: Ibzan Elon and Abdon: Three brief notes about judges who followed Jephthah: Ibzan of Bethlehem, Elon the Zebulonite and Abdon the Pirathonite.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Birth of Samson
scene: Birth of Samson: The angel of the Lord tells Manoah's wife, who is barren, that she will bear a son who is to be a Nazarite from birth and will begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Samson's marriage and riddle
scene: Samson's marriage and riddle: Samson wants to marry a Philistine woman of Timnath. On the way he kills a lion with his bare hands, and at the wedding feast he sets a riddle about honey from its carcass.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Samson's conflicts with Philistines
scene: Samson's conflicts with Philistines: Samson's quarrel with the Philistines escalates. He sets foxes with firebrands loose in their corn and kills a thousand men with the jawbone of an ass.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Samson and Delilah
scene: Samson and Delilah: Samson loves Delilah, and the Philistine lords pay her to discover the secret of his strength. When his hair is cut he is captured and blinded. In the temple of Dagon he prays for strength one last time.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Micah's idol and Danite migration
scene: Micah's idol and Danite migration: A man named Micah sets up idols and hires a Levite as his priest. The tribe of Dan, looking for land, takes both and conquers the city of Laish.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Levite's concubine and civil war
scene: Levite's concubine and civil war: The darkest story in Judges: a Levite's concubine is abused and killed at Gibeah of Benjamin, and the tribes go to war against Benjamin. The book ends,
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Naomi and Ruth return to Bethlehem
scene: Naomi and Ruth return to Bethlehem: Naomi loses her husband and two sons in Moab and decides to return to Bethlehem. Her daughter-in-law Ruth refuses to leave her.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Ruth meets Boaz
scene: Ruth meets Boaz: Ruth, a Moabite widow, goes to glean leftover grain in the fields to provide for her mother-in-law Naomi. She happens to come to the field of Boaz, a relative of Naomi's late husband.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Ruth at the threshing floor
scene: Ruth at the threshing floor: Naomi sends Ruth to the threshing floor at night to ask Boaz, a near kinsman, to take her under his protection. Boaz praises her kindness and promises to act.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Boaz redeems Ruth
scene: Boaz redeems Ruth: At the city gate, Boaz settles the matter of redemption with a nearer kinsman and marries Ruth. Their son Obed is the grandfather of David.
setting: the hill country and valleys of ancient Canaan: walled towns, fields and Israelite tribes

title: Hannah's prayer and Samuel's birth
scene: Hannah's prayer and Samuel's birth: Hannah, childless and provoked by her rival, prays at Shiloh so earnestly that Eli thinks she is drunk. She bears Samuel, gives him to serve the Lord, and sings a song of praise.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Eli's sons and judgment
scene: Eli's sons and judgment: Eli's sons, priests at Shiloh, treat the offerings of the Lord with contempt. Meanwhile the boy Samuel grows in favour, and a man of God brings word of judgment on Eli's house.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Samuel hears God's call
scene: Samuel hears God's call: The boy Samuel serves under the priest Eli at Shiloh. One night he hears a voice calling his name, and thinks it is Eli.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Ark captured by Philistines
scene: Ark captured by Philistines: Israel takes the ark of the covenant into battle, but the Philistines win and capture it. Eli's sons are killed, and Eli falls and dies when he hears the news.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Ark among the Philistines
scene: Ark among the Philistines: The Philistines put the ark in the temple of Dagon, and the idol falls before it. Plagues follow the ark from city to city, until the Philistines send it back on a new cart drawn by two cows.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Samuel leads Israel to repentance
scene: Samuel leads Israel to repentance: Samuel calls Israel to put away foreign gods and gathers them at Mizpeh. When the Philistines attack, the Lord thunders against them. Samuel sets up a stone and names it Ebenezer.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Israel demands a king
scene: Israel demands a king: Samuel is old and his sons are corrupt, so the elders ask for a king. God tells Samuel that they have rejected him, not Samuel, and Samuel warns them what a king will take.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Saul chosen and anointed
scene: Saul chosen and anointed: Saul, a tall young Benjamite, goes looking for his father's lost asses and comes to Samuel. Samuel anoints him privately, and later he is chosen by lot at Mizpeh while hiding among the baggage.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Saul rescues Jabesh-gilead
scene: Saul rescues Jabesh-gilead: Nahash the Ammonite threatens to put out the right eye of every man in Jabesh-gilead. The Spirit of God comes on Saul, he rallies Israel, and the city is saved. The kingdom is renewed at Gilgal.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Saul's unlawful sacrifice
scene: Saul's unlawful sacrifice: Facing a huge Philistine army, Saul's men begin to scatter. When Samuel is late, Saul offers the burnt offering himself. Samuel tells him his kingdom will not continue.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Jonathan attacks Philistines
scene: Jonathan attacks Philistines: Jonathan and his armourbearer climb up to a Philistine garrison alone, and panic spreads through the enemy camp. Saul's rash oath forbidding food nearly costs Jonathan his life.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Saul disobeys God
scene: Saul disobeys God: Saul is told to destroy Amalek completely, but he spares King Agag and the best of the livestock. Samuel tells him, and that the Lord has rejected him as king.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David anointed
scene: David anointed: God sends Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint one of Jesse's sons. Seven sons pass before him, but. The youngest, David, is called in from the sheep.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David serves Saul
scene: David serves Saul: The Spirit of the Lord departs from Saul and an evil spirit troubles him. David, is brought to play the harp, and Saul is refreshed.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David and Goliath
scene: David and Goliath: The Philistine champion Goliath challenges Israel's army for forty days. David, a young shepherd bringing food to his brothers, hears the challenge.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David and Jonathan's friendship
scene: David and Jonathan's friendship: After Goliath, Jonathan loves David, while Saul grows jealous as the women sing. Jonathan warns David with arrows shot in a field, and they part in tears.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David flees to Nob and Gath
scene: David flees to Nob and Gath: On the run, David asks Ahimelech the priest at Nob for bread and is given the hallowed bread and Goliath's sword. In Gath he pretends to be mad to escape King Achish.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Massacre of priests at Nob
scene: Massacre of priests at Nob: David gathers about four hundred men at the cave of Adullam. Doeg the Edomite tells Saul that the priests helped David, and Saul has them killed. Abiathar alone escapes to David.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David rescues Keilah
scene: David rescues Keilah: David asks the Lord and saves the town of Keilah from the Philistines, but must flee when its people would hand him over. Jonathan finds him in the wilderness and strengthens his hand in God.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David spares Saul in the cave
scene: David spares Saul in the cave: Saul goes into a cave at En-gedi where David and his men are hiding. David secretly cuts off the skirt of Saul's robe but will not harm. Saul weeps when he learns of it.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Abigail and Nabal
scene: Abigail and Nabal: David asks the rich and churlish Nabal for provisions and is insulted. David sets out for revenge, but Nabal's wise wife Abigail meets him with gifts and words that turn him back.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David spares Saul again
scene: David spares Saul again: David and Abishai creep into Saul's camp at night and take his spear and water jug as he sleeps. Again David refuses to harm Saul, and calls to him from the opposite hill.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David among Philistines
scene: David among Philistines: Despairing of escaping Saul, David takes refuge with Achish of Gath and is given the town of Ziklag. When the Philistines march against Israel, their lords refuse to let David fight with them.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David recovers captives at Ziklag
scene: David recovers captives at Ziklag: David returns to find Ziklag burned and the families taken by Amalekites. His men speak of stoning him, but, pursues the raiders and recovers everything.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Saul and the medium at Endor
scene: Saul and the medium at Endor: With the Philistines gathered and God silent, Saul disguises himself and visits a woman with a familiar spirit at Endor, asking her to bring up Samuel.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: The death of Saul and Jonathan
scene: The death of Saul and Jonathan: The Philistines defeat Israel on mount Gilboa. Saul's sons, Jonathan among them, are killed, and Saul himself dies. First Samuel and First Chronicles both record it; Chronicles adds why Saul died.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David mourns Saul and Jonathan
scene: David mourns Saul and Jonathan: An Amalekite brings David news of Saul's death, expecting a reward. David mourns and composes a lament for Saul and Jonathan:
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David becomes king over Judah
scene: David becomes king over Judah: David is anointed king over Judah at Hebron, while Abner makes Saul's son Ish-bosheth king over Israel. Their forces meet at the pool of Gibeon.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Civil war with Ish-bosheth
scene: Civil war with Ish-bosheth: A long war follows between the house of Saul and the house of David. Abner changes sides but is killed by Joab, and Ish-bosheth is murdered in his bed. David punishes the murderers.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David king over all Israel
scene: David king over all Israel: All the tribes come to David at Hebron and anoint him king over Israel. He is thirty years old and reigns forty years.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David captures Jerusalem
scene: David captures Jerusalem: David takes the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites, and it becomes the city of David. Hiram, king of Tyre, sends cedar and craftsmen to build David a house.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: The ark brought to Jerusalem
scene: The ark brought to Jerusalem: David brings the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem with music and dancing. On the way, Uzzah touches the ark and dies, and David waits three months before trying again. Chronicles gives the fuller account, with the Levites and their songs.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: God's covenant with David
scene: God's covenant with David: David wants to build a house for God. Through the prophet Nathan, God answers that he will build David a house instead: a lasting kingdom through David's offspring. David responds with a prayer.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David's victories
scene: David's victories: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, Zobah and Syria, and reigns with justice. He shows kindness to Jonathan's lame son Mephibosheth, who eats at the king's table.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David and Bathsheba
scene: David and Bathsheba: David stays in Jerusalem. He sees Bathsheba bathing, takes her, and when she is with child arranges the death of her husband Uriah in battle.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Nathan confronts David
scene: Nathan confronts David: The prophet Nathan tells David a story of a rich man who took a poor man's only lamb. David is furious, and Nathan says, David confesses, and the child dies. Solomon is born afterwards.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Amnon and Tamar
scene: Amnon and Tamar: David's son Amnon desires his half-sister Tamar, deceives her, forces her, and then hates her. Two years later her brother Absalom has Amnon killed and flees.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Absalom returns
scene: Absalom returns: Joab sends a wise woman of Tekoah to persuade David, through a story, to bring Absalom home. Absalom returns, but waits two years before he sees the king's face.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Absalom's rebellion
scene: Absalom's rebellion: Absalom steals the hearts of Israel and proclaims himself king at Hebron. David flees Jerusalem weeping. Hushai, David's friend, defeats the advice of Ahithophel at Absalom's court.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Death of Absalom
scene: Death of Absalom: David's army fights Absalom's in the wood of Ephraim. Absalom's head catches in an oak, and Joab kills him against the king's order. David weeps,
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David's grief and return
scene: David's grief and return: Joab rebukes David for mourning while his loyal men feel shamed. David returns to Jerusalem, pardons Shimei who had cursed him, and is met by Mephibosheth and old Barzillai.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Sheba's rebellion
scene: Sheba's rebellion: Sheba, a Benjamite, calls Israel away from David. Joab kills his rival Amasa and besieges Abel, where a wise woman ends the siege.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: David's census and the plague
scene: David's census and the plague: David orders a count of the fighting men of Israel, and then knows he has sinned. A plague follows, which stops at the threshing floor of Araunah, where David builds an altar.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Adonijah seeks the throne
scene: Adonijah seeks the throne: As David lies old and frail, his son Adonijah declares himself king. Nathan and Bathsheba remind David of his promise, and Solomon is anointed and rides on the king's mule.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Solomon becomes king
scene: Solomon becomes king: David gives Solomon his final charge to walk in God's ways and dies after reigning forty years. Solomon secures his throne, dealing with Adonijah, Joab and Shimei.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Solomon asks for wisdom
scene: Solomon asks for wisdom: God appears to the young King Solomon in a dream at Gibeon and says, Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Solomon judges two mothers
scene: Solomon judges two mothers: Two women come before Solomon, each claiming the same living baby. He orders a sword to divide the child, and the true mother gives up her claim to save it.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Building the temple
scene: Building the temple: Solomon builds the house of the Lord in Jerusalem with cedar from Lebanon and craftsmen from Tyre. Kings and Chronicles both describe the work and its furnishings in detail.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: The temple dedicated
scene: The temple dedicated: The ark is brought into the finished temple and the glory of the Lord fills the house. Solomon blesses the people and prays a long prayer of dedication.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: God appears to Solomon
scene: God appears to Solomon: After the temple is finished, God appears to Solomon a second time with a promise and a warning. Solomon gives cities to Hiram and builds up his kingdom.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: The queen of Sheba
scene: The queen of Sheba: The queen of Sheba hears of Solomon's fame and comes to test him with hard questions. She sees his wisdom and his court, and blesses the Lord his God.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Solomon's downfall
scene: Solomon's downfall: Solomon loves many foreign women, who turn his heart after other gods in his old age. God tells him the kingdom will be torn from his son, and raises up adversaries, among them Jeroboam.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: The kingdom divided under Rehoboam
scene: The kingdom divided under Rehoboam: After Solomon's death, the people ask his son Rehoboam to lighten their burdens. He takes the advice of the young men instead of the old, and ten tribes turn to Jeroboam. The kingdom divides into Israel in the north and Judah in the south.
setting: the kingdoms of ancient Israel and Judah: Jerusalem, stone palaces and walls, Iron Age dress and armour

title: Jeroboam's golden calves
scene: Jeroboam's golden calves: Jeroboam, king of the northern tribes, fears that his people will return to Jerusalem to worship. He sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan, saying.
